title: Alert Onboarding: Tenant-default Policies & Template Library (brainstorm)
content:
Context / goal:
- Problem: customers struggle to pick sensible alerting defaults when they first enable SLO monitoring. They either copy noisy defaults from other vendors or leave everything to 'email', causing operator overload.
- Goal: create an onboarding flow + small library of editable alert templates + clear tenant-level default policy model so teams get reasonable alerts out-of-the-box and can customize with low effort.

Assumptions / constraints:
- Must be simple for first-time users (3 clicks to get 'good' defaults) but powerful for advanced users (policy composer with chaining and overrides).
- Support multi-tenant orgs: org-level defaults (security/compliance), tenant-level defaults (team preferences), route/monitor overrides (service owners).
- Integrate with existing channel types: Slack, MS Teams, Email, PagerDuty, Opsgenie, webhooks, SMS (third-party).
- Keep UI consistent with Console's existing rollouts/notifications pattern (left rail navigation, top context bar).

Sketch: Onboarding wizard (wireframe notes)
- Step 1: "Scope" — ask: Which services will you monitor? (simple tag input; suggest 'frontend', 'api', 'payments' sample tags).
- Step 2: "SLO profile" — choose from presets: "User-critical (low error budget)", "Business-critical (medium)", "Non-critical (high)". Each maps to default SLO targets and alert thresholds.
- Step 3: "Notify defaults" — choose default channels: Primary (Pager/PD), Secondary (Slack), Digest (email daily). Allow copy from org defaults. Show estimated weekly alert count based on historical traffic (if available).
- Step 4: Review & finish: shows summary of template selections and link to template editor.

Template library (what each template contains)
- Name: short, human-friendly (e.g. "High-error spike - page-impacting").
- Severity mapping: P0/P1/P2 presets.
- Trigger: SLO breach vs SLI spike vs prompt regression. Support compound rules: e.g., "error_rate > 2% for 5m AND p50_latency > 300ms".
- Channels: ordered list with escalation windows. e.g. P0 -> PagerDuty immediate -> Slack #oncall -> SMS fallback after 10m.
- Suppression: time-of-day quiet-hours settings and on-call calendar integration.
- Example templated message: "[{{severity}}] {{service}} - {{slo_name}} breached: {{value}} (> {{threshold}}) — link". Variables must be documented.

Tenant-default policy model (draft)
- Layers (precedence high->low):
  1) Route/Monitor level override (service owner explicitly sets).
  2) Tenant-level policy (team defaults configured during onboarding).
  3) Org-level policy (security/compliance enforced)
- Enforced fields: org-level can mark channels as required/forbidden (e.g., forbid SMS for PII teams), or set min severity for PagerDuty.
- Tenant-level policies are editable via console and can be cloned per new service.

Policy composer UX ideas (mini wireframe)
- Left: condition builder (drag/drop clauses: metric, window, comparator, duration).
- Middle: rule summary + immediate preview (textual rule: "When error_rate > 1% for 3m -> severity = P1").
- Right: notification chain editor (cards for channel + delay + escalation). Cards have quick toggles: "urgent (pager)" vs "digest (email)".
- Quick actions: "auto-suggest" uses SLO history to propose thresholds and estimated alert counts.

Onboarding defaults (suggested presets)
- Starter pack (low-noise): P0 (SLO burn > 50% in 5m) -> Pager + Slack. P1 (5% SLO burn in 1h) -> Slack + Email digest. P2 (monthly SLO degradation) -> Email digest only.
- Aggressive pack (sensitive teams): lower thresholds, more immediate escalations.
- Quiet pack (platform infra teams): more aggregation and digest style.

Edge cases and open questions (TODO)
- How to calculate "estimated weekly alert count" without exposing private metrics? Use aggregated sampling + opt-in telemetry.
- Should tenant onboarding allow templated import from GitHub/terraform? Many customers want infra-as-code for alerting.
- How to model cross-tenant on-call rotations (shared PD services)? Need mapping UI to organization-level PD integration.
- Quieter default for newly onboarded services (start in 'observe' mode for 7 days before paging). Should be opt-out.

Example templated messages (copyable)
- Short: "[P0] {{service}}: {{slo}} breached — {{current}} > {{threshold}} ({{window}}). Investigate: {{runbook_url}}"
- Verbose (Slack thread opener): "Alert: {{service}} — {{slo}} — severity {{severity}}. Observed {{metric_series}}. Recent commits: {{last_commits}}. Suggested play: {{playbook}}"

Acceptance criteria (for initial MVP)
- Onboarding wizard with 3 steps + option to skip and open template library.
- Template library page with CRUD for templates and tenant-level defaults.
- Policy composer that supports: single metric threshold, duration, and notification chain with delays.
- Clear precedence rules documented in console help text.
- 'Observe mode' flag when creating a new monitor (7-day no-page default).

Next actions / owners
- UX: Marco to create mockups for the onboarding screens + composer by 2025-01-20.
- Backend: Priya to spec API for tenant-defaults and policy precedence (PLAT-9876) by 2025-01-24.
- Integrations: Jamal to validate PD & on-call calendar mapping constraints (contacts + escalation groups) by 2025-01-28.

Notes to self:
- Keep the template names short and avoid vendor-specific wording.
- We should include a "bulk-apply" flow for tenant defaults to apply to existing monitors (preview diffs).
- Build in telemetry to measure "time-to-first-pager" and "first-week alert volume" for onboarded services.

Links and references:
- Confluence: CNF-12345 (Alert template guidelines)
- Jira: PLAT-9876 (tenant-defaults API)
- UX inspiration: Grafana/Alertmanager onboarding flows (notes in UX board)

Unresolved UX trade-offs:
- Inline composer vs full-screen composer: inline is faster but limited; full-screen supports advanced chaining. Maybe offer a compact composer and "open full editor" link.
- How many presets to surface? 3 seems right for clarity but allow "advanced" selection.

End of doc.

(Brainstorm / working doc — expect many edits; keep short bullets and wireframe callouts in this file rather than polished mockups.)
